cosine/cos: Cosine decay glides along a curve called the cosine, written cos. Feed it pi, a number about three point one four, times t over T. As t runs from zero to T, the cosine of pi t over T falls from one to minus one: slowly, then fast, then slowly.
cosine/vals: Along the way, a third of the way through, it is a half. Halfway, it is zero. Three quarters of the way, it is about minus zero point seven one.
cosine/halve: Add one and halve it, and the curve runs from one down to zero instead: a third of the way, zero point seven five; halfway, a half.
cosine/scale: Stretch it across the gap from the top rate, eta max, to the bottom one, eta min, and add the bottom. The rate at step t, eta t, is eta min plus half the gap, times one plus the cosine.
cosine/half: From zero point one down to zero, half the gap is zero point zero five. Halfway through, the cosine is zero, so the rate is zero point zero five times one: zero point zero five.
cosine/third: A third of the way in, the cosine is a half, so the rate is zero point zero five times one point five: zero point zero seven five.
both/both: Runs often join the two: warm up over the first k steps, then decay along the cosine over the next T, counting its t from the end of the warmup.
both/ex: Warm up to zero point one over a thousand steps, then decay to zero over three thousand. Step two thousand five hundred is fifteen hundred steps into the decay: halfway, where the cosine is zero. So the rate is zero point zero five.
try/p1: Try one: cosine decay from zero point one down to zero point zero one over twelve hundred steps. What is the rate at step nine hundred? Use a cosine of about minus zero point seven zero seven.
try/a1: Nine hundred over twelve hundred is three quarters of the way. The cosine there is about minus zero point seven zero seven, so one plus it is zero point two nine three.
try/a2: Half the gap is half of zero point zero nine: zero point zero four five. Times zero point two nine three, that is about zero point zero one three two. Add the bottom, zero point zero one: about zero point zero two three two.
